channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Apple and Google avoid binding DMCC commitments, critics call proposals “lightweight”
item.description: The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority has secured voluntary commitments from Apple and Google to deliver greater transparency and “fairness” across their mobile ecosystems, but critics say the agreements amount to “lightweight” steps unlikely to “materially shift” competition.

item.title: UK consumer protection collective action regime could fill enforcement gap, ex-enforcer says
item.description: “Wedging” consumer claims into competition cases is “breaking" the UK’s class action regime, the former deputy general counsel at the Competition and Markets Authority has warned.

item.title: Justice league: The Tipline for 10 February 2026
item.description: The Department of Justice has taken down a man of steel using the Sherman Act rather than kryptonite. The Antitrust Division and US Department of Defense’s inspector general investigation ended with the president of Gulfstream Steel & Supply pleading guilty to rigging bids submitted to the US military. Also in Tipline, Amazon seeks to dismiss California’s pricing parity case.

item.title: Paramount races for merger clearance, adds to WB offer
item.description: Paramount has said it largely completed the Department of Justice’s second request just two months after launching a $108 billion hostile bid for Warner Bros Discovery.

item.title: Full time: The Briefing for 11 February 2026
item.description: Real Madrid and UEFA are set to end their legal dispute stemming from the European Super League fallout after the parties announced an “agreement of principles” today. The Spanish football club, which was the last remaining team still signed up to the failed breakaway league, had previously said it was seeking around €4.5 billion in antitrust damages from European football’s governing body for ban...

item.title: US DOJ files landmark CFIUS divestment suit
item.description: The US Department of Justice has sued a Chinese company for failing to divest a local tech business it acquired six years ago, despite an order from President Donald Trump detailing national security concerns.

item.title: US treasury targets known investors in CFIUS consultation
item.description: The US Department of the Treasury is seeking views on how to streamline the country’s foreign investment screening processes, specifically targeting the Known Investor Programme.

item.title: Innsworth granted judicial review in Merricks settlement
item.description: A UK court has allowed litigation funder Innsworth Advisors to challenge certain aspects of the Competition Appeal Tribunal’s distribution plan for the landmark £200 million opt-out collective action settlement between Walter Merricks and Mastercard.

item.title: Staying power: The Tipline for 11 February 2026
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission’s insulin pricing case will remain paused. After finalising a settlement with Express Scripts last week, FTC staff said they are in talks with CVS Caremark and OptumRx – the remaining pharmacy benefit manager defendants – about a resolution. Also in Tipline, an $85 million judgment for illegal tying of emissions-reducing tech is upheld.

item.title: DOJ and Live Nation seek to squash Ticketmaster merger testimony
item.description: The antitrust markets defined in the Department of Justice’s approval of Live Nation/Ticketmaster are “irrelevant” to the monopolisation trial scheduled for next month, the Antitrust Division has argued.
